summary: Frontend verification of the MFA setup / owner-account bug fix. Full 8-step Playwright flow passed: (1) new customer registered via /login (Cadastro mode, birth_date 1990-01-01); (2) owner session injected via mongosh, then POST /api/admin/staff promoted the new account to staff → 200 {ok:true}; (3) fresh login with the promoted staff account correctly shows the MFA SETUP screen — data-testid=mfa-qrcode (react-qr-code SVG), data-testid=mfa-secret (32-char base32) and data-testid=mfa-code are all visible with heading 'Ative o MFA' and the disclaimer 'O MFA só será ativado após você informar um código válido gerado pelo app.'; (4) invalid TOTP '000000' → sonner toast 'Código inválido' and user remains on the setup screen (mfa-qrcode still visible), meaning MFA is NOT flipped to enabled; (5) owner login mgrodrigues920@gmail.com with wrong password → 401 {detail:'Credenciais inválidas'} — no MFA state leak; (6) forgot-password link on /login navigates to /esqueci-senha and renders forgot-email input; (7) regression: plain customer registration lands directly on /conta without any MFA prompt; (8) mobile 390x844: /login has NO horizontal overflow (sw=cw=390). Also verified require_admin still returns 401/403 with invalid/no MFA — retained customer JWT after promotion cannot use admin endpoints until mfa_enabled=true (backend correctly re-derives role+MFA from DB per request).

design_issues.screen: Header navigation on the MFA setup screen
issues: Immediately after login as a freshly-promoted staff (before completing MFA setup), the top nav already renders the 'Painel Admin' link and 'Olá, {name}' greeting because AuthContext's /auth/me sees the retained customer JWT with the new role from DB. Access is correctly blocked by require_admin (needs mfa_enabled=true), but the visible admin link is misleading UX — consider gating the Painel Admin link on user.mfa_enabled as well.

action_items: (Optional UX) Hide 'Painel Admin' link in the top nav when user.role∈{owner,staff} but user.mfa_enabled=false — otherwise clicking it just yields a 403 from the admin API.
critical_code_review_comments: Owner mgrodrigues920@gmail.com currently still has mfa_enabled:true with a stale mfa_secret in DB (JGXDEB...MDG). This is the exact residue the bug report described — it will only be cleared when the owner actually runs the forgot-password flow (server.py /auth/reset-password wipes MFA). Until then the real owner cannot log in without the residual TOTP secret and MUST use 'Esqueci minha senha'. This matches the documented recovery path in /app/memory/test_credentials.md but is worth flagging so the human owner knows to run the password-reset flow.

AuthContext.login() correctly avoids setUser/setToken when the response is mfa_required/mfa_setup_required (no token in payload), but the previously-set customer JWT in localStorage still authenticates /auth/me and yields the new staff role. Combined with require_admin's MFA gate this is safe, but the UX is slightly leaky (see design_issues).

server.py grant_staff correctly revokes user_sessions on role change but does NOT bump password_version, so a pre-existing JWT for that user remains valid across the promotion. Not a security issue given the MFA gate, but worth noting.
test_credentials: Owner: mgrodrigues920@gmail.com — real password unknown to testing agent; use forgot-password. Automated admin session: inject users doc with role='owner' + mfa_enabled:true and a matching user_sessions doc (see /app/auth_testing.md).
seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up in-run: users teste.staff.1789421673@example.com, teste.cliente.1789421673@example.com, teste.owner.1789421638@example.com and matching test_adm_session_1789421638. Final mongosh cleanup deleted all users matching ^teste. and all sessions starting with test_. Zero test residue remaining.
context_for_next_testing_agent: MFA setup UI works exactly per spec: mfa-qrcode (SVG QR from react-qr-code), mfa-secret (base32 chunk), mfa-code input, mfa-verify-btn, and the disclaimer 'O MFA só será ativado após você informar um código válido gerado pelo app.'. To test the SUCCESS path of MFA verification you need a real TOTP — call the backend directly: (a) POST /api/auth/login → get mfa_token; (b) POST /api/auth/mfa/setup {mfa_token} → get secret; (c) compute TOTP via pyotp.TOTP(secret).now(); (d) POST /api/auth/mfa/verify {mfa_token, code} → real JWT + recovery_codes array. Alternatively drive it through the browser by pasting the pyotp-computed code into data-testid=mfa-code. Owner mgrodrigues920@gmail.com STILL has stale mfa_enabled:true + mfa_secret in DB until the human triggers the password-reset flow — expected per fix design.
rca of the issue: Original bug: mgrodrigues920@gmail.com received an MFA-code prompt without ever seeing the QR setup screen because a previous automated test had already flipped mfa_enabled:true and stored a test-only mfa_secret on the real owner account. Fixes verified from the frontend perspective: (i) LoginPage now renders a full setup screen (QR + manual key + explanatory copy) whenever the backend responds with mfa_setup_required, driven by react-qr-code — confirmed by screenshot; (ii) MFA activation is guarded server-side by requiring a valid TOTP before flipping mfa_enabled — confirmed by invalid-code toast + persistent setup screen; (iii) password reset clears MFA residue (backend-only, not exercised end-to-end here because it requires opening the reset email); (iv) mfa_token alone does not gain admin access — require_admin gates on DB mfa_enabled=true regardless of any token used. No new defects found.
